en.title: Princess Donut Cast! Dungeon Crawler Carl Series Finds Its Star
en.summary: The highly anticipated Peacock adaptation of the beloved LitRPG series Dungeon Crawler Carl has officially cast its most iconic feline. This casting choice hints at a faithful adaptation that fans will adore.
en.body:
The journey into **Peacock**'s **Dungeon Crawler Carl** adaptation is taking a significant step forward, with the announcement that **Jeff Hays** has been cast as the one and only Princess Donut. This revelation, made at SDCC 2026 by **Matt Dinniman**, is a major win for fans who have been eagerly awaiting any news about the series' development. Hays is no stranger to the world of **Dungeon Crawler Carl**; he is the acclaimed narrator and producer of the series' incredibly popular audiobooks, bringing the chaotic and hilarious adventures of Carl and Donut to life with his distinctive voice.

For those unfamiliar with the phenomenon that is **Dungeon Crawler Carl**, the series began its life as a hit within the LitRPG genre before exploding into mainstream popularity, largely thanks to its dedicated fanbase. At its heart, the story follows Carl, a man thrust into a deadly, interdimensional dungeon crawl after a mysterious cataclysm. Accompanying him is Princess Donut, a rather regal and surprisingly resourceful show cat (full name Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk). Far from being a mere sidekick, Princess Donut undergoes significant transformations and development throughout the dungeon, evolving into one of the series' most beloved and complex characters. The fact that her casting was confirmed before Carl's own speaks volumes about her fan-favorite status and the importance of capturing her unique essence for the screen.

## A Beloved Character Takes Center Stage

The casting of **Jeff Hays** as Princess Donut is more than just a piece of news; it's a powerful signal to the **Dungeon Crawler Carl** community. Fans have long championed Princess Donut, appreciating her sharp wit, unexpected bravery, and the sheer absurdity of her presence in a life-or-death dungeon. Hays's intimate knowledge of the character, honed through his audiobook work, suggests a deep understanding of what makes Princess Donut so special. This choice hints that the **Peacock** series aims to honor the source material's spirit and character dynamics, a move that will undoubtedly be met with widespread approval from the passionate fanbase who were instrumental in the books' ascent to bestseller status.

## What's Next for the Dungeon Crawl

While the casting of Princess Donut is a monumental development, details about the wider cast, including who will play Carl, and specific production timelines remain under wraps. Fans will be watching closely for further announcements as **Peacock** continues to build out this ambitious adaptation, hoping for a release date that allows them to return to the dungeon soon.

Hays will undoubtedly be a familiar name to fans of the Dungeon Crawler Carl books. He not only narrates the series’ audiobooks but produces them as well. While this is the only confirmed bit of casting for the series so far, it at least suggests that the show is going to stick fairly close to its source material wherever possible. If so, that would hardly be a surprise given how much its fans contributed to this series going from an entry in the still somewhat obscure LitRPG genre to a full mainstream hit. And if you are not a Dungeon Crawler Carl fan, then just know that Princess Donut is a prized show cat (full name Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk) who accompanies Carl on his journey into the mysterious dungeon that appears following a transformative event. Much like Carl, Princess Donut undergoes quite a few changes in the Dungeon and emerges as one of the series’ best characters. The fact that Princess Donut was cast before Carl in the series kind of says something about the character’s fan-favorite status. On that note, we really still don’t know much about that series outside of what was initially revealed relative ages ago . It’s going to premiere on Peacock, Matt Dinniman is creatively involved, and the series is produced by Seth MacFarlane’s Fuzzy Door. It seems likely that the series will make it to production given how absurdly popular the books have become, but we’ve of course seen stranger things happen in the world of literary adaptations.
